scenario.description: An assistant principal must finalize a response and re-entry plan for a student who violated a laboratory safety rule, with input from the science teacher, school counselor, and school psychologist.

shared_context.S1: A student intentionally discharged a fire extinguisher during a chemistry period, causing the room to be evacuated and closing the laboratory for the rest of the day.
shared_context.S2: The current draft response recommends a two-day out-of-school suspension followed by an ordinary return to class.
shared_context.S3: Ms. Brooks has authority to finalize the disciplinary response and re-entry plan.
shared_context.S4: As part of the school's weekly conduct review, Ms. Brooks routinely asks the involved teacher, counselor, and psychologist for relevant information before finalizing a response.
shared_context.S5: The conduct-review routine requires each consultant to place any recommendation based on their own records, family contact, or completed assessment on the record before Ms. Brooks settles the plan; the consultant identifies the source and the specific action it supports.

PF1.text: Mr. Shah's classroom observation log shows that the student accepted a restorative conference and repaired damaged materials after a prior safety incident; he recommends replacing the draft's two-day out-of-school suspension with exactly one day of in-school restorative conference, but the observation log has not yet been attached to the conduct referral.

PF2.text: Ms. Molina confirmed with the student's guardian that an in-person meeting is impossible because of a recurring work shift, while a phone meeting at exactly 6:30 p.m. is available; the family-contact preference has not yet been entered in the conduct plan.

PF3.text: Dr. Ellis's risk review requires a 20-minute adult check-in every school day for exactly 10 school days and prohibits the student's unsupervised access to the chemistry laboratory for exactly 5 school days after return; the review is complete but has not yet been uploaded to the student-support record.

acceptance_conditions: The response must be exactly one day in an in-school restorative conference.
The guardian meeting must be by phone at exactly 6:30 p.m.
The student must receive a 20-minute adult check-in every school day.
The check-in must continue for exactly 10 school days.
The student must not have unsupervised chemistry-laboratory access for exactly 5 school days after return.
A restorative-plan commitment must be recorded.
A family-contact commitment must be recorded.
A safety-monitoring commitment must be recorded.

content_checks.C1: decisions['disciplinary_days'] == 1 and ('restorative conference' in decisions['disciplinary_setting'] or decisions['disciplinary_setting'] == 'in_school_restorative_conference')
content_checks.C6: decisions['disciplinary_days'] == 1 and 'restorative' in decisions['disciplinary_setting'] and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids
content_checks.C7: any('family' in c and 'contact' in c for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any('risk review' in c or 'safety' in c and 'monitor' in c for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The prior successful repair response changes the disciplinary fields from the draft's two-day out-of-school suspension to exactly 1 day with a restorative-conference setting, and supports citing PF1 for that change.
The guardian's confirmed work conflict changes the meeting method to a phone meeting at exactly 6:30 p.m. and supports a family-contact commitment.
The completed risk review changes the re-entry fields to exactly 20 minutes, exactly 10 school days, and exactly 5 restricted-access days, and supports a risk-review or safety-monitoring commitment.
